boards.title: Your First Weekend at Merrimack College, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key first-weekend sequence that moves from settling in and meeting people to campus recreation, arts, and an optional local errand run.

cards.title: Start with a Hub check-in
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · behind the Sakowich Campus Center
cards.notes: Stop by the Hub to ask OSI staff about current programs, student organizations, and ways to join campus activities before making weekend plans.
cards.short_summary: A practical first stop for current student-life information.
cards.evidence_claim: Merrimack identifies the Hub, behind the Sakowich Center, as a place to speak with Office of Student Involvement staff about making the most of campus life.
cards.access_notes: The Hub lists weekday hours of Monday–Friday, 8:30 a.m.–5 p.m.; plan this stop during those hours.

cards.title: Get your bearings at Sakowich
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · campus center
cards.notes: Use the building directory to locate dining, recreation, the chapel, commuter lounge, and student-support offices so later stops feel familiar.
cards.short_summary: One building links several everyday campus resources.
cards.evidence_claim: The Sakowich Campus Center houses dining, recreation, student services, and gathering spaces for the Merrimack community.
cards.access_notes: Check the campus center directory or information desk for current room access and event availability.

cards.title: Make a dinner plan at Sparky’s
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · Sakowich Campus Center
cards.notes: Review the current menu and hours, then use an eligible meal swipe or another accepted payment method for a straightforward first campus dinner.
cards.short_summary: A named dining hall in the Sakowich Campus Center.
cards.evidence_claim: Merrimack lists Sparky's Place in the Sakowich Campus Center and states that meal swipes can be used there.
cards.access_notes: Menu and operating hours are published through Merrimack Dining; confirm them before going.

cards.title: Try a low-pressure game night
cards.subtitle: Friday night · lower level of the Collegiate Church of Christ the Teacher
cards.notes: Meet up in the Student Union and choose bowling, pool, golf simulation, or the gaming area; ask the front desk about any needed sign-up.
cards.short_summary: A social campus space with several non-alcohol-focused activities.
cards.evidence_claim: Merrimack describes the Student Union as a campus social space with bowling, billiards, a golf simulator, and an esports gaming area.
cards.access_notes: Published weekend hours are Saturday–Sunday, 10 a.m.–11 p.m.; hours are subject to change.

cards.title: Queue up in the esports room
cards.subtitle: Friday night · Student Union
cards.notes: If gaming is your thing, bring a few new hallmates to the dedicated esports area; the published FAQ says it needs no reservation.
cards.short_summary: A distinct game room inside the Student Union.
cards.evidence_claim: Merrimack's Student Union includes a dedicated esports area with PCs, Xbox Series X consoles, Nintendo Switch devices, and Oculus VR; its FAQ says esports are free and require no reservation.
cards.access_notes: The published Student Union weekend hours list pool tables and esports from 10 a.m.–11 p.m.; hours are subject to change.

cards.title: Reset at McQuade Library
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · 315 Turnpike Street
cards.notes: Pick a group workspace or quiet corner, explore MACKsearch, and save the library contact options for when a course assignment needs research help.
cards.short_summary: A study-and-research anchor for the rest of the semester.
cards.evidence_claim: McQuade Library provides group work spaces and quiet study corners, and offers research assistance through librarians.
cards.access_notes: Consult the library's current hours calendar before visiting.

cards.title: Fit in a first-year-quad workout
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · lower level of Deegan West Hall
cards.notes: Use the 47 Fitness Center for a short independent cardio or strength session, then make a note of its location for between-class workouts.
cards.short_summary: A named fitness space located in the first-year quad.
cards.evidence_claim: Merrimack describes 47 Fitness Center as an accessible workout space in the first-year quad with cardio machines, strength equipment, and open floor space.
cards.access_notes: Published hours are Sunday–Thursday, 5 a.m.–midnight, and Friday–Saturday, 5 a.m.–9:30 p.m.; hours may change during breaks or special schedules.

cards.title: Look for a gallery or performance
cards.subtitle: Saturday evening · Rogers Center for the Arts
cards.notes: Check the Rogers Center calendar and gallery information before heading over; choose an exhibition or performance that fits your weekend schedule.
cards.short_summary: A campus arts destination with performance programming and two galleries.
cards.evidence_claim: The Rogers Center for the Arts houses the McCoy and Thagaste galleries and presents arts programming for the campus community.
cards.source_title: Rogers Center for the Arts | Merrimack College
cards.access_notes: Ticketing and exhibition access vary by event; review the Rogers Center listing before attending.

cards.title: Take the weekend shuttle for essentials
cards.subtitle: Sunday · campus pickup to local stops
cards.notes: Use the published weekend route for an errand run, and confirm the live schedule before leaving campus because routes and times can change.
cards.short_summary: A free college-operated ride connecting campus with local errand stops.
cards.evidence_claim: Merrimack states that the Warrior Shuttle is free for students and that its weekend Blue Line serves McQuade Library, CVS, Market Basket, Andover Landing, Shawsheen Plaza, and LaRosa's Cafe.
cards.access_notes: Weekend service is listed separately for Saturday and Sunday; use the current Blue Line schedule or live tracker before departure.

cards.title: Put the Involvement Fair on your radar
cards.subtitle: Next fall-semester campus event
cards.notes: When the fair is scheduled, walk through with one goal: collect details for a few groups you would genuinely try rather than signing up everywhere.
cards.short_summary: A recurring way to meet organizations and campus resources.
cards.evidence_claim: Merrimack describes the fall Student Involvement Fair as an opportunity for new and returning students to meet organizations, clubs, offices, and campus resources.
cards.access_notes: The event is a fall-semester program; consult the upcoming campus calendar for its current date and location.
